o1: Enables G protein activity; G protein-coupled acetylcholine receptor activity; and GTP binding activity. Predicted to enable GTPase activity. Involved in detection of cold stimulus involved in thermoception; negative regulation of cholinergic synaptic transmission; response to monoamine; establishment of spindle orientation; asymmetric cell division; cytokinesis; and mitotic spindle positioning. Is located in cell cortex. Is expressed in several structures, including neurons; non-striated muscle; pharynx; spermatheca; and vulva. Is part of the G-protein signaling pathway, including heterotrimeric G-protein signaling pathway. Used to study developmental and epileptic encephalopathy and early infantile epileptic encephalopathy. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 17 and neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements. Orthologous to human GNAO1 (G protein subunit alpha o1).
